sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十多岁的心理学》，在这个播客中，我们讨论二十多岁时最大的改变、时刻和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理学的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It's so great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能在这里见到你们。

sentences.en: As always, back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，欢迎收看新的一期节目，我们将剖析二十多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: At this stage, our 30s and beyond.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，我们甚至要探讨三十多岁及以后。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about the psychology of compatibility and what makes people write for each other on a very, very fundamental level, on an emotional level.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊相容性的心理学，以及是什么让人们在非常、非常基础的层面上、在情感层面上真正契合彼此。

sentences.en: There is so much about dating and about falling in love that feels entirely up to chance.
sentences.zh: 在约会和坠入爱河的过程中，有太多事情感觉完全取决于运气。

sentences.en: It is so rare to even meet somebody that you like and for them to like you back and to then create a relationship, and that comes with a great deal of vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 能够遇到一个你喜欢而且对方也喜欢你的人，然后建立起一段关系，这是极其罕见的，而这需要付出巨大的情感脆弱。

sentences.en: So when all of that finally happens, I think we naturally want to assume that just being with somebody must mean we're compatible,
sentences.zh: 所以，当这一切终于发生时，我想我们自然会认为，只要和某人在一起就一定意味着我们是相容的，

sentences.en: but after a while, sometimes these little things come up that make us question if we really are.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，有时这些小事情会出现，让我们质疑我们是否真的是天生一对。

sentences.en: There is this initial level of compatibility, which is, you know, I like the same music, everything feels easy, we're attracted to each other.
sentences.zh: 存在着这样最初级别的相容性，也就是，你知道的，我喜欢同样的音乐，一切都感觉很轻松，我们互相吸引。

sentences.en: But then there's also a secondary, deeper level, which is do we believe in the same things?
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有一个次要的、更深层次的级别，那就是我们是否有相同的信仰？

sentences.en: Do we believe in the same good in the world?
sentences.zh: 我们是否相信世上有同样的善？

sentences.en: Are our values aligned?
sentences.zh: 我们的价值观是否一致？

sentences.en: Do I want to be with this person?
sentences.zh: 我想和这个人在一起吗？

sentences.en: Do I want this person to be a present force in my life for 10, 5, 15, 50 years?
sentences.zh: 我希望这个人成为我生命中持续10年、5年、15年、50年的常驻力量吗？

sentences.en: I think a lot of compatibility is a lot less glamorous than what we make it to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为相容性其实远没有我们想象的那么光鲜亮丽。

sentences.en: It's a lot of work, and it's a lot of something else that people don't really speak about.
sentences.zh: 它需要付出很多努力，而且还包含许多人们并不怎么谈论的其他东西。

sentences.en: So today I want to just break down the literature on this.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天只想剖析一下关于这方面的文献。

sentences.en: The past 30 years, researchers and psychologists have done so much research and so much experimentation into what makes relationships last, what doesn't,
sentences.zh: 在过去的30年里，研究人员和心理学家做了大量的研究和实验，探讨是什么让关系长久，什么不会，

sentences.en: what is the secret sauce amongst those who do.
sentences.zh: 那些维持长久关系的人们的秘密武器到底是什么。

sentences.en: And so I want to summarize it all today and maybe help you out in whatever stage of a relationship you are in right now, whether you are currently looking
sentences.zh: 因此，我想在今天总结这一切，并或许能对你有所帮助，无论你目前处于关系的哪一个阶段，无论你是在寻找伴侣

sentences.en: and want to make a good choice, whether you feel like you've in fact found your soulmate and want to just validate that, or maybe if you have a few doubts,
sentences.zh: 并希望做出一个好的选择，还是觉得自己确实找到了灵魂伴侣并只想加以印证，又或许你心中存有那么一些疑虑，

sentences.en: I think that this episode is going to provide every single person listening with something that they maybe don't know about how two people find each other
sentences.zh: 我认为这一集将为每一个倾听的听众提供一些他们可能不知道的知识，关于两个人是如何找到彼此的，

sentences.en: and how two people make it work and whether that is a choice or whether it is destiny.
sentences.zh: 以及两个人是如何让关系运作的，这究竟是一种选择还是命中注定。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology of compatibility.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入相容性的心理学。

sentences.en: When we look at the psychology literature, as I was saying, on what makes people compatible, two categories emerge.
sentences.zh: 当我们查阅心理学文献时，正如我刚才所说，关于是什么让人与人相容，出现了两个类别。

sentences.en: There is the category of things which people think make people compatible and which we often focus on excessively in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 一类是人们认为能让人相容的事物，这也是我们在开始时往往过度关注的。

sentences.en: And then there is the category of less sexy things that actually make people want to be with each other in the long run.
sentences.zh: 另一类则是那些不那么性感、但实际上能让人们长久相处下去的事物。

sentences.en: These are a lot less flashy.
sentences.zh: 这些要低调得多。

sentences.en: They're also harder to recognize.
sentences.zh: 它们也更难以辨认。

sentences.en: I think a lot of them reveal themselves over time.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中很多需要随着时间的推移才会显现出来。

sentences.en: So the first meeting might not always give you the best indication of whether you and somebody else are going to last, maybe not even the 10th or the 15th date,
sentences.zh: 所以第一次见面并不总能给你提供最好的迹象，表明你和另一个人能否长久，甚至第10次或第15次约会也未必能说明问题，

sentences.en: maybe not even the second or the third year.
sentences.zh: 甚至第二年或第三年也可能看不出来。

sentences.en: Let's run through these separately, starting with the factors we think matter moSt.
sentences.zh: 让我们分别过一遍这些因素，从我们认为最核心的因素开始。

sentences.en: I would say this includes things like physical attraction.
sentences.zh: 我想这包括诸如身体吸引力之类的东西。

sentences.en: It includes the spark.
sentences.zh: 它包括那种火花。

sentences.en: And it also includes personality, which may come as a shock that personality doesn't matter as much as we think it does, but it actually doesn't.
sentences.zh: 它还包括个性，这可能会让人感到震惊，因为个性并不像我们想象的那么重要，但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk about that a little bit more later on.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会对此进行更多讨论。

sentences.en: But firstly, physical attraction.
sentences.zh: 但首先，是身体吸引力。

sentences.en: How much of whether two people make it comes down to thinking that somebody else is just hot?
sentences.zh: 两个人能否走到一起，有多大程度上取决于觉得对方很有魅力？

sentences.en: Very little.
sentences.zh: 微乎其微。

sentences.en: You could probably answer that for yourself, but very little.
sentences.zh: 你大概自己也能回答这个问题，答案是微乎其微。

sentences.en: I remember doing a sex ed class when I was in high school and we had like, I don't know if your sex ed did this, but we had the opportunity to ask our health teacher
sentences.zh: 我记得我在高中时上过一堂性教育课，我们有——我不知道你们的性教育课是不是这样，但我们有机会向我们的健康老师

sentences.en: like anonymous questions using like a piece of paper and a pen and he'd like pick it out of a bowl.
sentences.zh: 用纸笔匿名提问，然后他会从碗里抽出来读。

sentences.en: And this was a middle-aged sports teacher.
sentences.zh: 那是一位中年体育老师。

sentences.en: He was like a bona fide bachelor.
sentences.zh: 他就像是个名副其实的单身汉。

sentences.en: And somebody asked him, what matters more, looks or personality?
sentences.zh: 有人问他，外表和个性哪个更重要？

sentences.en: Which is a very earnest question to ask as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 对于一个青少年来说，这是一个非常真诚的问题。

sentences.en: And I remember very distinctly him giving us the most straight answer any adult had probably ever given us.
sentences.zh: 我清晰地记得他给出了任何成年人可能给过我们的最直截了当的回答。

sentences.en: He was essentially like,
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，

sentences.en: I'm not going to lie to you, looks matter a lot.
sentences.zh: 我不会对你们撒谎，外表非常重要。

sentences.en: They matter a lot when you were young.
sentences.zh: 当你们年轻时，它们非常重要。

sentences.en: They matter less as an adult.
sentences.zh: 等你长大了，它们的重要性就会降低。

sentences.en: When you get to around the age of 30,
sentences.zh: 当你大约30岁的时候，

sentences.en: values matter more.
sentences.zh: 价值观变得更为重要。

sentences.en: And I remember being like 16 and being like, well, that sucks.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时自己16岁，心想，好吧，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I've got a while to wait.
sentences.zh: 我还得等好一阵子呢。

sentences.en: But he was actually partially correct.
sentences.zh: 但他的确有部分是对的。

sentences.en: When researchers ask people of different ages to rank what attributes are most important to them in a partner, in our 20s and 30s, physical attraction sits actually pretty high,
sentences.zh: 当研究人员让不同年龄段的人对伴侣身上最重要的特质进行排序时，在我们20多岁和30多岁时，身体吸引力实际上排名相当高，

sentences.en: near the top of the liSt.
sentences.zh: 位于清单的顶端附近。

sentences.en: But the older we get, it falls continuously with each decade.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们年龄的增长，它在每一个十年里都在持续下降。

sentences.en: And I think this represents a shift from external to like internal value and a change of priorities.
sentences.zh: 我认为这代表了一种从外部价值向内部价值的转变，以及优先事项的变化。

sentences.en: Like somebody being hot or beautiful, that's great.
sentences.zh: 就像某人很火辣或很漂亮，这很棒。

sentences.en: But do you want to go into debt with this person?
sentences.zh: 但你想和这个人一起背负债务吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to endure the worst moments of your life with them?
sentences.zh: 你想和他们一起度过你生命中最糟糕的时刻吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to hate them at times?
sentences.zh: 你有时候会想恨他们吗？

sentences.en: I think that like we see looks for what they really are, which is shallow,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们开始看清外表的真面目，也就是肤浅、

sentences.en: something that fades, and something that doesn't actually give an indicator of what comes underneath.
sentences.zh: 会消逝的事物，以及并不能真正指示内在的事物。

sentences.en: Physical attraction is what we would call a dating motivator, but it's not relationship fuel.
sentences.zh: 身体吸引力是我们所说的约会驱动力，但它不是关系的燃料。

sentences.en: You know, the evolutionary theory is that we are more attracted to people we deem as having greater mating potential.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，进化理论认为，我们更容易被那些我们认为具有更高繁殖潜力的人所吸引。

sentences.en: That's what the theory says.
sentences.zh: 这就是该理论的观点。

sentences.en: We're more attracted to people who we think will produce healthier offspring.
sentences.zh: 我们更容易被那些我们认为能孕育出更健康后代的人所吸引。

sentences.en: Nowadays, we know that that theory is very outdated because people are attracted to all kinds of other people who probably wouldn't make a great parent, right?
sentences.zh: 如今，我们知道这个理论已经非常过时了，因为人们会被各种各样其他人所吸引，而这些人可能并不是好父母，对吧？

sentences.en: Like there's all these other explanations now that seem to take precedent.
sentences.zh: 就像现在有所有这些其他的解释似乎占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: What researchers now do suggest is that physical attraction is subjective and it's based, yes, loosely on physical health and fitness, but it's really based on preferences.
sentences.zh: 研究人员现在所表明的是，身体吸引力是主观的，是的，它大致基于身体健康和体能，但它实际上基于偏好。

sentences.en: It's based on upbringing.
sentences.zh: 它基于成长环境。

sentences.en: And what it is inevitably is a hook that enables a spark to develop between people or more so, it's something that like gives people a basis to meet and therefore to bond.
sentences.zh: 不可否认的是，它是一个诱饵，能够让人们之间产生火花，或者更确切地说，它为人们提供了一个相遇并进而建立联系的基础。

sentences.en: It is physical attraction is bait that's hopefully going to help you find something deeper about that person that you like.
sentences.zh: 身体吸引力是一种诱饵，希望能帮你发现该身上更深层次你所喜爱的东西。

sentences.en: In fact, having an instantaneous, complete drug-like attraction to somebody may actually mean you avoid noticing fundamental differences that hurt you down the line.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对某人产生瞬时的、完全像药物一样的吸引力，实际上可能意味着你忽略了以后会伤害你的根本差异。

sentences.en: We all glamorize this idea of like love at first sight, but studies show couples who experience highly passionate, fast-moving courtships, often called like Hollywood romances,
sentences.zh: 我们都把一见钟情这种想法浪漫化了，但研究表明，经历高度激情、进展迅速的恋爱关系（通常被称为好莱坞式的浪漫）的人，

sentences.en: actually tend to grow dissatisfied much quicker and they face a higher statistical probability of divorcing within seven years of marrying compared to those who didn't have that
sentences.zh: 往往会更快地感到不满，并且在结婚后七年内离婚的统计概率更高，相比之下，那些在开始时没有

sentences.en: like hot and heavy spark at the beginning but did have a longer courtship, did seem to actually build chemistry over time.
sentences.zh: 那种炽热火花，但恋情持续时间更长、确实随时间建立起化学反应的人而言更是如此。

sentences.en: It also becomes easy
sentences.zh: 这也变得很简单，

sentences.en: if you are only looking for attraction to be infatuated by the idea of somebody else and infatuated by the idea that somebody else likes you.
sentences.zh: 如果你只寻找吸引力，就会对外表产生迷恋，并对别人也喜欢你的这种想法产生迷恋。

sentences.en: To explain that a little bit better, there was a 2009 study published in the Journal of Personality Psychology and what it found was that people find others most attractive
sentences.zh: 为了更好地解释这一点，2009年《人格心理学杂志》上发表了一项研究，发现人们发现其他人最具吸引力的时候，

sentences.en: And for the couples who inevitably got divorced, the conversation always began with really harsh criticism.

sentences.zh: 对话总是始于厌恶或蔑视，而且双方都没有试图缓和局势。

sentences.en: These couples always got divorced.
sentences.zh: 这些夫妇最终都离婚了。

sentences.en: In the couples who stayed married, they started their conversation with humor, with goodwill, with generosity, and they both deescalated.
sentences.zh: 而在那些保持婚姻的夫妇中，他们的对话是以幽默、善意和慷慨开场的，并且双方都缓和了冲突。

sentences.en: There was a huge difference between you are so lazy and you never do anything.

sentences.en: That difference is what they, they basically simply concluded was that difference is the divorce rate.

sentences.zh: 其中有一种是最糟糕的。如果在一段关系中存在这四种中的任何一种，戈特曼夫妇基本上就会认为，这里必须采取措施了。

sentences.en: So the first was criticism.
sentences.zh: 所以第一种是批评。

sentences.en: This was when a complaint about something your partner has done becomes an attack on who they are as a person.

sentences.en: It is the difference between, I wish you had told me you were going to be late and you never think about anybody but yourself.

sentences.en: That's the split.

sentences.en: And once somebody feels like, well, this person already thinks that I'm a loser, it's very hard to be receptive to changing what you think stems from that loserness, right?

sentences.en: The problem is, is that defensiveness, just like criticism, maybe not as bad, leaves literally no room to like actually work on a problem together.

sentences.en: And so essentially what the Gottman said was that when you get to the stage, the problem solving like has left the building.

sentences.en: It also just might be, of all of these different ones, like it is the one that kind of happens incidentally and because somebody's trying to protect themselves.

sentences.en: What you really need to look at is how does somebody treat you when you fight with them?

sentences.en: What I found so interesting is that, especially in our 20s, like we don't want to fight with our partner.

sentences.en: Like when you're in the early stages of a relationship,

sentences.en: you really just want to look at all the fun stuff.

sentences.en: And it's actually the ugliest parts of a relationship where you are really going to know whether this person is with you for the long term.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，恰恰是在一段关系中最丑陋的部分，你才能真正知道这个人是否会长期和你在一起。

sentences.en: Again, it made me think about a lot of these claims from people that like, we never fight, we've never had a disagreement.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这让我想起了很多人宣称的那些话，比如“我们从不吵架，我们从来没有分歧”。

sentences.en: That used to seem like, to me, the best sign that these guys were like going to make it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这过去似乎是这些人能够长久走下去的最佳征兆。

sentences.en: Like, wow, these people don't fight?
sentences.zh: 就像，哇，这些人不吵架？

sentences.en: They must be the best couple in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们一定是对世界上最好的伴侣。

sentences.en: But one final paper I want to talk about essentially says that if you don't fight, you are
sentences.zh: 但我想谈的最后一篇论文基本上指出，如果你不吵架，你就

sentences.en: missing out on some of the best information you will ever get about the other person, which is what do they really think about me?
sentences.zh: 会错过关于对方的最宝贵的信息，那就是：他们究竟是怎么看我的？

sentences.en: And can I see myself in their eyes as they're arguing with me?
sentences.zh: 当他们在和我争吵时，我能在他们的眼泪或眼神中看到自己吗？

sentences.en: Like, what do they, how are they going to treat me at the worst point?
sentences.zh: 就像，他们在最糟糕的时候会怎么对待我？

sentences.en: So this paper that I'm referring to was published in 2013.
sentences.zh: 我提到的这篇论文发表于2013年。

sentences.en: It was a paper by Campbell and colleagues in the Journal of Personality and
sentences.zh: 这是坎贝尔及其同事发表在《人格与

sentences.en: Social Psychology.
sentences.zh: 社会心理学杂志》上的一篇论文。

sentences.en: And what they did was they brought married couples into the lab.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是把已婚夫妇请进实验室。

sentences.en: And like the Gottman study, they had them discuss an unresolved problem in their relationship for about 12 minutes.
sentences.zh: 就像戈特曼的研究一样，他们让夫妻双方花大约12分钟讨论他们关系中尚未解决的问题。

sentences.en: And they, and the researchers filmed them and they talked about, you know, do we want kids, messiness, family, money?
sentences.zh: 研究人员拍摄了他们，他们讨论了，你知道的，我们要不要孩子、凌乱、家庭、金钱？

sentences.en: What they found was that conflict acted as what they call a diagnostic situation.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，冲突起到了他们所谓的“诊断情境”的作用。

sentences.en: When somebody felt that their partner fell short of their ideals, particularly around warmth and trustworthiness, they behaved more negatively, they behaved less positively.
sentences.zh: 当一个人觉得自己的伴侣达不到他们的理想（尤其是在温暖和诚实守信方面）时，他们表现得更加消极，表现得更不积极。

sentences.en: And their partner picked up on that.
sentences.zh: 而他们的伴侣察觉到了这一点。

sentences.en: They picked up on the fact that like, you're not treating me well.
sentences.zh: 他们察觉到了这样一个事实，即你对我不够好。

sentences.en: After the conflict, that caused them to adjust their, their perception of how they believed their partner saw them based on the way they had just been treated.
sentences.zh: 冲突过后，这导致他们根据刚刚受到的对待，调整了对自己认为伴侣如何看待自己的感知。

sentences.en: In other words, we are surprisingly good at reading between the lines of an argument and detecting what does our partner really think about us?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们出奇地擅长从争吵的字里行间读出弦外之音，并探测出伴侣对我们到底是怎么看的？

sentences.en: Like, what are we arguing over because it's because of the subject?
sentences.zh: 就像，我们争吵是因为事情本身吗？

sentences.en: And what are we arguing over because of us?
sentences.zh: 还是我们争吵是因为我们自己？

sentences.en: This is the big resounding conclusion to this entire episode.
sentences.zh: 这是整期节目最响亮的结论。

sentences.en: It is very easy to be in love when you're on holiday, when you are, have just met, when you are having fun, or it's a good time in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 当你在度假时，当你刚认识时，当你正在享受乐趣时，或者在关系的蜜月期，坠入爱河是非常容易的。

sentences.en: But all that tells us actually is very little.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些其实并不能说明什么。

sentences.en: It doesn't tell you much about the future.
sentences.zh: 它并不能告诉你太多关于未来的事。

sentences.en: When your partner is really angry at you, when you are furious, when you feel betrayed, when there is something that like you just can't like

sentences.en: communicate, do they still treat you with respect?

sentences.en: Do they still love you even when they fundamentally disagree with you or dislike you?

sentences.en: I want to finish with one final study from 2020.

sentences.en: It's perhaps one of the most comprehensive ever done on this entire subject, which is what makes love laSt. And it essentially summarizes all the points we've made today.
sentences.zh: 这可能是关于整个主题（即是什么让爱持久）的最全面的研究之一，它基本上总结了我们今天提出的所有观点。

sentences.en: It was a study by Joel and colleagues that looked at 11,000 couples, so almost 20,000 people.
sentences.zh: 这是乔尔及其同事的一项研究，调查了11000对伴侣，也就是将近20000人。

sentences.en: And it essentially said, the people who like each other have a few things in common.
sentences.zh: 它基本上表明，那些彼此相爱的人有几个共同点。

sentences.en: Whether they are at year five or year 50 of their relationship, they, A, felt like
sentences.zh: 无论他们处于关系的第五年还是第五十年，他们：A，觉得

sentences.en: their partner was committed to them for better or for worse without marriage at times, like with or without marriage.
sentences.zh: 他们的伴侣无论好坏都对这段关系承诺，无论是否结婚，就像结不结婚都一样。

sentences.en: They just felt like they were committed.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得对方是坚定向自己承诺的。

sentences.en: B, they felt appreciated.
sentences.zh: B，他们感到被感激。

sentences.en: C, they felt like the other person was happy.
sentences.zh: C，他们觉得对方是快乐的。

sentences.en: And D, they fought and they fought well.
sentences.zh: D，他们会吵架，而且吵得很好。

sentences.en: Look at that.
sentences.zh: 看吧。

sentences.en: That's literally it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: All my talking, all my jabbering, and one study summarizes it all.
sentences.zh: 我说了这么多，唠叨了这么多，一个研究就把它们全概括了。

sentences.en: But that is essentially the crux of compatibility.
sentences.zh: 但这就是契合度的核心所在。

sentences.en: Do I like you even when I don't like you?

sentences.en: I'm going to end this episode with a caveat though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我将在本集结束时加上一个前提。

sentences.en: I love looking at the research.

sentences.en: I love examining the numbers and the data and the trends.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢审视数字、数据和趋势。

sentences.en: But in every single study, there are always people without a doubt who don't fit the mold.
sentences.zh: 但在每一项研究中，总会有那么一些人毫无疑问地不符合这个模子。

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 总是有的。

sentences.en: Psychology is such an imperfect science at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 说到底，心理学是一门非常不完美的科学。

sentences.en: Like we really like, we like to believe that we as humans all act the same and we follow the same rules and that we can scientifically determine what those
sentences.zh: 就像我们真的喜欢——我们喜欢相信我们人类的行为方式都是一样的，我们遵循相同的规则，我们可以通过实验科学地确定那些

sentences.en: rules are using experiments.
sentences.zh: 规则是什么。

sentences.en: Or if you and your partner are actually exactly alike and you're both introverts and you're both conscientious and you're both agreeable, you share the exact same, I don't know,
